title: Explicit backoff envelope and idempotency surface for multiplexed tool streams
author: Leah Park
description:
Motivation: We have intermittent client-visible failures for streamed tool/function invocations when upstream rate-limit signals are ambiguous (mix of Retry-After, X-RateLimit-Reset-Ms, and vendor-specific headers) and when multiple tool streams are multiplexed over the same connection. This causes incorrect retry timing, duplicate tool execution, and opaque error surfaces in the OpenAI-compat adapter. This PR introduces an explicit "backoff envelope" parity layer and a clearer idempotency session surface for streamed tool calls, providing deterministic retry behavior and structured error codes that SDKs can rely on.

What this change does (summary):
- Adds a BackoffEnvelope: standardized parsing and canonicalization of rate/ retry signals from upstream responses (supports Retry-After, Retry-After-Ms, X-RateLimit-Reset-Ms, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Quota, and vendor backoff headers). The envelope yields: canonical_retry_after_ms, rate_window_ms, and priority_hint.
- Introduces Idempotency Session tokens for multiplexed streaming tool invocations. When a streaming request declares tool/function calls, the adapter issues/accepts an idempotency_session_id that scopes retries to the logical stream session (prevents duplicate tool side-effects across reconnects).
- Stream framing guards: stronger delimiters and sequence checks for partial-frame error payloads so SDKs can detect partial tool responses and trigger safe replays only when the session idempotency state permits it.
- Structured error codes: map common runtime cases into an explicit error_code field (examples: "rate_limited", "retryable_transient", "permanent", "partial_result"), plus backoff_hint_ms where applicable. This is surfaced in the OpenAI-compat adapter response envelope and in the runtime internal error model.
- SDK + doc updates: small changes in the Python/TS SDKs to consume idempotency_session_id, follow backoff_hint_ms, and expose structured errors to callers. Docs page added with migration guidance and examples.

Compatibility and policy:
- Backward compatible: adapter continues to accept existing headers; when no canonical signal is present we fall back to conservative defaults. New idempotency_session_id is optional for clients; if the client does not supply it, the adapter will assign one but will not change behaviour for single-shot non-streamed calls.
- Safety: idempotency_session_id semantics are conservative by default: only retries that the adapter can prove to be safe (no committed tool side-effects) will re-execute; otherwise the adapter returns a structured error with "partial_result" and a backoff_hint_ms.

Testing and verification:
- Unit tests for header parsing and canonicalization (header permutations, bad values, clock skew compensation).
- E2E streaming tests that simulate network reconnects, mixed 429/503 patterns, and vendor headers.
- Integration tests with the python SDK to verify session idempotency behaviour and correct error-code propagation.
- A small perf benchmark ensures no material change to steady-state latency for non-retry flows (observed ~0.2% median overhead in decode path under test).

Rollout plan:
- Feature-flagged behind runtime flag: runtime.openai_compat.backoff_envelope (default off for 48 hours in staging).
- Canary rollout to 10% of hosted traffic for 72 hours with alerts for: unexpected duplicate tool invocations, increased 5xx rate, and higher latency tail for streamed requests.
- If stable, flip default on and follow with SDK + docs announcement.

Files changed (high level):
- server/adapter/openai_compat/headers.go: new canonicalizer for backoff headers and utils for clock skew safe parsing.
- server/adapter/openai_compat/stream_decoder.go: framing guards and session rehydration hooks.
- server/adapter/openai_compat/idempotency.go: idempotency session lifecycle and safe-replay predicates.
- sdk/python/openai_compat_client.py: client opt-in for idempotency_session_id and helpers to honor backoff_hint_ms.
- docs/openai-compat/backoff-idempotency.md: migration guide and examples.
- test/e2e/streaming_tool_idempotency_test.go: new end-to-end test harness scenarios.

Checklist:
- [x] Header parsing robust against malformed inputs and clock skew
- [x] Idempotency session respects tool side-effect safety rules
- [x] SDKs consume new fields and expose structured errors
- [x] CI/E2E passing (flaky streaming tests stabilized)
- [x] Migration docs and rollout plan attached

Notes: This PR focuses on correctness and deterministic behavior for retries in multiplexed streamed workloads. Subsequent PRs will add telemetry counters to track idempotency session reuse and per-tool replay counts to refine automatic replay heuristics.

review_comments: Diego Martinez: Can you clarify how we handle clock skew between upstream server and runtime? Response: headers.go applies a conservative floor of 250ms plus skew window (configurable); parsing normalizes to ms and rejects negative values.
Sara Chowdhury: Suggest making idempotency_session_id TTL configurable per-tenant; Response: added tenant-configurable TTL (defaults 10m) and documented in runtime config.
Evan Holt: Are there any perf implications for high QPS multiplexed streams? Response: bench shows ~0.2% decode overhead; added micro-optimizations to reuse buffer slices in decoder.
QA: Observed a flaky e2e case where partial frames returned without error_code; Response: updated framing guards to synthesize 'partial_result' with backoff_hint_ms when the stream ends unexpectedly.
approvals: Diego Martinez: approved — tests and canary plan look good

release_notes: Added a canonical backoff envelope and idempotency session tokens for streamed tool/function calls. SDKs can opt in to idempotency_session_id and should honor backoff_hint_ms and structured error_code fields. Rollout behind feature flag and canaried before full release.
examples: Client: set headers { 'Idempotency-Session': '<uuid>' } to scope retries to a streaming tool session
Adapter: response includes { 'error_code': 'rate_limited', 'backoff_hint_ms': 12000 } for callers to respect
